rationale: Pre-revenue nuclear developer with investor attention but no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship offers little commercial logic.

name: Persistent Systems
desc: Provides software development, digital engineering, cloud, data and AI services to clients in banking, healthcare, software and telecom.
markets: Clients mainly in the United States plus Europe and Asia; large offshore delivery base in India.
rationale: IT services firm whose peers Cognizant and Mphasis already sponsor F1; offers client hospitality and brand visibility in the US and Europe.

name: Quantinuum
desc: Builds trapped-ion quantum computers and software such as InQuanto for enterprises, governments and researchers.
markets: Enterprise, government and research customers; operations in the US and the UK.
rationale: Deep-tech firm with limited consumer awareness; F1 could provide a technology showcase and client hospitality, but fit is modest.

name: Rapido
desc: Operates an Indian ride-hailing app for bike taxis, autos and cabs, and delivery services, in over 100 cities.

name: SandboxAQ

markets: Enterprise and government customers in life sciences, chemicals and defence, mainly US-based.
rationale: Deep-tech B2B brand with low consumer awareness; F1 could be a technology showcase but enterprise sales are specialised.

name: Sierra

markets: Large consumer brands and telecoms as customers, mainly in the US; international reach not verified here.
rationale: Enterprise AI start-up with consumer-brand customers; F1 could provide hospitality for client brands but awareness is limited to tech circles.

name: Supabase
desc: Provides an open-source backend platform with a Postgres database, authentication, storage and real-time APIs for application developers.
markets: Developers and start-ups worldwide on usage-based and subscription plans.
rationale: Developer-focused brand with strong community appeal but little mainstream marketing; F1 fit is limited to technology audiences.

name: Temporal Technologies
desc: Offers the open-source Temporal platform for durable workflow execution, used by developers to build reliable distributed applications and AI agents.
markets: Developer and enterprise customers mainly in the US; international reach not verified here.
rationale: Developer infrastructure brand with no consumer marketing; F1 offers little beyond a technology showcase.

name: Tyler Technologies
desc: Provides software and services for courts, property tax, public safety and payments to US state and local governments.
markets: US state and local governments; no significant international operations known.
rationale: Government-facing software vendor with low public brand awareness; F1 sponsorship is a poor match.

name: ClickHouse
desc: Develops the open-source ClickHouse column-oriented analytics database and sells it as a managed cloud service.
markets: Developers and enterprises worldwide, with customers such as Cloudflare, Uber and eBay.
rationale: Developer and data-engineering brand; F1 data-heavy racing offers a technology showcase, though marketing appetite is unproven.

name: 4iG
desc: Hungarian technology group providing IT services and system integration, owning telecom operator One Hungary and defence and space businesses.

name: Advanced Machine Intelligence (AMI Labs)

markets: Pre-revenue research lab in Paris; no commercial products or verified international operations.

name: Al² Robotics
desc: Chinese robotics company developing robots, according to Crunchbase; products, customers and ownership are not confirmed.
markets: Shenzhen base; customers and any international plans are not confirmed.

name: Apptronik
desc: Designs and builds the Apollo general-purpose humanoid robot for logistics and manufacturing, spun out of the University of Texas.

rationale: Humanoid robotics brand with growing media attention; F1 could be a technology showcase, but products are early-stage.

name: Bedrock Robotics
desc: Retrofits excavators and other heavy construction machines with autonomous operating systems for building contractors.
markets: US construction contractors only; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Early-stage B2B construction technology with no consumer brand; F1 is a poor fit apart from technology credibility.

name: CAIS

markets: Independent financial advisers, mainly in the United States; international reach not verified here.

name: Cart.com
desc: Provides e-commerce fulfillment, logistics, marketing and software services to online direct-to-consumer and B2B brands.

name: Clear Street
desc: Provides cloud-native clearing, prime brokerage, securities lending and trading infrastructure for hedge funds, institutional traders and retail brokers.
markets: Hedge funds, institutions and brokers, mainly in the United States; international reach not verified here.

name: Commure
desc: Offers ambient AI clinical documentation, revenue cycle automation and workflow tools to hospitals and physician groups.

rationale: Healthcare software vendor with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship offers little reach to hospital buyers.

name: Domyn
desc: Develops responsible AI for regulated industries such as finance, insurance and government, including the Colosseum supercomputer and Magnum model.
markets: Enterprise and public-sector customers, mainly in Italy; international plans not verified here.

name: Galaxy Bot (Galbot)
desc: Develops embodied AI and general-purpose humanoid robots, including wheeled robots for retail and pharmacy settings.
markets: Retailers, factories and logistics operators in China; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Early-stage Chinese robotics firm with little brand marketing; F1 could be a technology showcase but the commercial fit is weak.

name: GeneDx
desc: Provides exome and genome sequencing and genetic tests, mainly for rare diseases and children's health, to hospitals and physicians.

markets: Pre-revenue London lab with no products on the market; no verified international operations.
rationale: Research-stage lab with no products or consumer brand; an F1 partnership has little commercial logic yet.

desc: US AI and robotics company reported to be linked to Rivian founder RJ Scaringe, developing AI for industrial robots.
markets: US-based developer for manufacturing robots; customers and international plans are not confirmed.
rationale: Early-stage B2B robotics developer with no consumer brand; an F1 fit is unproven.

desc: Builds satellites and ground systems for Earth observation, navigation, telecom and science missions for space agencies and governments.

rationale: Government-facing space manufacturer with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship is a poor match.
